ActionChunk.description: A sequence of instantaneous command steps at a fixed period, typically from a policy.

steps.description: Commands per step; one per addressed component.

AppliedCommand.description: What a runtime actually applied for one execution's command. The command as

execution.description: Execution identifier; its Submission holds the command.

modifications.description: Every change between the submitted and applied command; empty if none.

ArrayValue.description: Dense array such as an image. Stored out of line as a content-addressed asset.

Attachment.description: A scene object declared held by an end effector.

transform.description: The object's pose in the end effector's frame.

allow.description: Robot frames and scene fixtures the object may touch, sorted.

held.description: False once the runtime reported the object left the grasp.

AttachmentViolation.description: A runtime's report that an attached object left its declared transform.

stamp.description: When the tolerance was first exceeded.

BasePoseGoal.description: Bring a mobile base's frame to a world pose.

pose.description: The base frame's goal pose in the world.

BaseTwistCommand.description: Planar velocity for a mobile base, expressed in the base's own frame.

linear.description: Forward (x) and leftward (y) velocity in the base frame.

angular.description: Counter-clockwise yaw rate about base z.

name.description: Channel name, unique within the robot.

source.description: Observed entity: a joint group (joint quantities), a gripper (opening), a frame (pose), a force-torque sensor (wrench), a camera (images), or, for a runtime's scene channels, a scene object (pose) or one entity of a contact.

frame.description: Reference frame a pose is expressed in; pose only.

privileged.description: Simulator truth a real robot could not supply, such as an object's true pose; false for what a robot's own sensors provide.

counterpart.description: The second entity of a contact channel; contact only.

ConfigurationGoal.description: Reach any one of these configurations of the request's joints.

configurations.description: Goal configurations, one value per joint in group order.

Contact.description: A contact that makes a planning-scene configuration invalid.

first.description: A description frame, scene object or fixture, or 'world'.

second.description: A description frame, scene object or fixture, or 'world'.

ContinuationReport.description: Whether a continuation ran, and the evidence for that decision.

prediction.description: Fingerprint of the prediction it was planned on.

plan.description: Fingerprint of the plan made on the prediction.

actual.description: Fingerprint of the captured arrival state.

predicted_start.description: The plan's start, from the prediction.

discrepancies.description: Every checked quantity outside its tolerance.

max_start_gap.description: The largest gap between the predicted and actual start.

rest_tolerance.description: The most a joint may still move, per second.

object_tolerance_m.description: How far a free object may have moved.

object_tolerance_rad.description: How far a free object may have turned.

rest_stamp.description: When the joint-velocity reading that established rest was valid: never before the arrival snapshot.

rebase.description: The planner's account of its rebase: any bridge or change.

rebased_plan.description: Fingerprint of the rebased plan, if there is one.

prepared.description: Fingerprint of the compiled PreparedTrajectory, if any.

execution.description: The continuation's execution identifier, if submitted.

Diagnostic.description: Why something was rejected, failed, or modified.

Discrepancy.description: One way the actual state differs from the prediction.

what.description: A joint, an object or its rotation, or 'revision'.

tolerance.description: The tolerance it was held to.

EffectiveLimits.description: The velocity and acceleration limits a motion must respect: the description's

ExecutionCheck.description: One independent check of a runtime command.

detail.description: The worst case found, with its bound.

ExecutionStatus.description: The state of one submitted command at a point in runtime time.

execution.description: Execution identifier, unique within a context.

diagnostic.description: Required for rejected, timed-out, and failed states.

guard.description: How a guarded trajectory ended; on its succeeded status only.

gripper.description: How a gripper command's motion ended; on its succeeded status only.

opening.description: 0 is fully closed, 1 is fully open.

GripperResult.description: How a ``GripperCommand`` execution's motion ended. The gripper keeps its target

requested_opening.description: The target opening in effect, after any clipping.

final_opening.description: The measured opening when it ended.

GuardCapability.description: Guarded trajectories a runtime executes for one component, and the timing it

component.description: The joint group whose trajectories may be guarded.

channels.description: Wrench channels a guard may read, sorted.

tare.description: Whether it measures from the reading at the start.

stop_latency_ns.description: Longest time from a triggering reading to the hold.

GuardOutcome.description: How a ``GuardedJointTrajectory`` ended, with the evidence to reproduce the

elapsed_ns.description: Time since the trajectory started when it ended.

part.description: Which half of the wrench was measured.

measure.description: The guarded measure at the deciding tick: the last of window.

baseline.description: The tare reading, untared, if the guard tares.

window.description: The last readings evaluated, untared, oldest first: the guard's samples, or every one if fewer were evaluated.

GuardedJointTrajectory.description: A ``JointTrajectory`` executed as usual until its guard triggers. The runtime then

InvalidWitness.description: The first invalid state found, where it is, and why.

segment.description: Interval index, for a motion or path.

time_s.description: Time into the trajectory, for a trajectory.

constraint.description: Index of the violated path constraint.

JointCommand.description: Instantaneous targets for every joint of a group, in the group's declared order.

joints.description: Joint names; must equal the group's order.

values.description: One value per joint, in the unit fixed by mode.

JointTrajectory.description: Timed joint positions for a group, executed from the time it starts.

joints.description: Joint names; must equal the group's order.

time_from_start_ns.description: Waypoint times; start at 0 and strictly increase.

positions.description: One row of joint positions per waypoint.

velocities.description: Optional row of joint velocities per waypoint.

MotionValidation.description: One validator's answer for one exact subject: valid under the reported policy, or

motion.description: Fingerprint of the exact subject; see *_identity.

interpolation.description: How a motion or path is interpolated.

intervals.description: Intervals in the subject: 0 for a state.

validator.description: Who answered, and under what policy.

valid.description: Whether the subject is valid under the policy.

witness.description: The first invalid state; present exactly when invalid.

evidence.description: For a trajectory validated along its source path, that path's identity (path_identity). Evidence, not part of the subject: the policy says how it is used.

ObjectState.description: A scene object's pose in the world.

pose.description: The object's pose in the world frame.

Observation.description: A set of readings assembled at one runtime time.

OffsetGoal.description: Move the request's frame in a straight line: ``distance`` along ``direction`` in

direction.description: Unit direction of motion in the world.

position_tolerance.description: Allowed distance from the line and the goal.

rotation_tolerance.description: Allowed rotation from the reference orientation, per axis.

reference_pose.description: World pose of the constrained frame at zero distance: its position anchors the line, its orientation is the one kept. None: the frame's pose at the request's start.

PlanningRequest.description: Everything a planner needs, fully resolved: who plans, from where, to what, under

snapshot.description: Fingerprint of the snapshot it plans in.

component.description: The manipulator or mobile base that moves.

start.description: The joints' positions in the snapshot.

frame.description: The frame pose goals and path constraints constrain, if any.

path_constraint.description: Regions frame must stay inside throughout; all apply.

constraints.description: Every constraint class the motion must satisfy, sorted.

seed.description: Random seed; equal requests give equal results.

clearance_m.description: Minimum separation the moving robot and its held objects keep from the environment, beyond allowed contacts; see docs/planning.md.

Pose.description: A rigid transform: the pose of a child frame expressed in a parent frame.

quat_wxyz.description: Unit quaternion (w, x, y, z) rotating child axes into parent.

PoseGoal.description: Bring the request's frame to a world pose, within tolerances.

pose.description: The frame's goal pose in the world.

position_tolerance.description: Allowed distance from the goal position.

rotation_tolerance.description: Allowed rotation from the goal orientation, per axis.

PredictedSnapshot.description: The state expected if ``source`` succeeds and every recorded assumption holds.

state.description: The predicted state, as a snapshot value; never a captured one.

base.description: Fingerprint of the captured snapshot it extends.

base_revision.description: The scene revision of that snapshot; a prediction adds no scene change.

command.description: Fingerprint of the source execution's command.

moved.description: The joints the source commands, at its last waypoint in the state.

held.description: Held objects whose predicted pose moves with the hand, as in the state.

unsettled.description: Free objects whose pose it makes no claim about, such as one just released and still falling: kept at their captured pose for planning, and not compared on arrival. The continuation is still validated whole in the actual scene.

expected.description: Joints the source does not move whose positions in the state the caller expects when the plan runs, such as a gripper's, opened by a release; for planning only. Only the plan's own joints are compared on arrival.

releases.description: Objects held by the source, expected to be released after it and before the plan made on it runs: the one scene change the prediction expects. In the state they are detached, at the resting pose the caller expects, for planning only; on arrival each must be detached, and is not compared by pose.

world.description: The world identity (model and scene) it is a state of.

lineage.description: Fingerprints it was predicted from, oldest first: the captured base.

PreparedTrajectory.description: A runtime command compiled from a timed trajectory: the readiness checks it

request.description: The request it was planned for.

source.description: The source trajectory's identity (trajectory_identity), which it samples.

contract.description: The trajectory-execution contract it was compiled for.

source_validation.description: The validator's report for the source trajectory.

compiled_validation.description: The same validator's report for the command, as a linear path.

geometry_preserved.description: Whether the command traces exactly the validated source path.

Reading.description: One channel's value with its own freshness.

stamp.description: When the value was valid, on the runtime clock.

value.description: Flat float64 values for vector quantities, else an array.

source_stamp.description: Original device timestamp, when it differs from stamp.

RuntimeHealth.description: A runtime's report that it faulted or recovered.

stamp.description: When the change happened, on the runtime clock.

components.description: Affected components; empty means the whole robot.

RuntimeInfo.description: What an opened runtime reports about itself.

clock.description: Clock identity used by every timestamp it produces.

description.description: Fingerprint of the bound robot description.

objects.description: Scene objects that can be attached, sorted; empty without a scene.

fixtures.description: Static scene bodies an attachment may allow contact with, sorted.

trajectory.description: How it executes a JointTrajectory; None if it declares no contract, so timed plans cannot be compiled for it.

guards.description: Per component, which force-torque guards it evaluates and how fast it stops, sorted by component; empty if it cannot execute a GuardedJointTrajectory.

scene_channels.description: Channels the runtime declares for its scene, such as each object's pose and each contact pair asked for; their names are also in channels.

privileged.description: Every confirmed channel, the robot's or the scene's, that is privileged simulator truth, sorted.

SceneSnapshot.description: An immutable copy of everything a geometric query reads: the robot's joint

runtime.description: Name of the runtime that captured it.

model.description: The runtime's identity for the simulated world; opaque to the core.

stamp.description: When it was captured, on the runtime clock.

revision.description: Scene revision it was captured at.

positions.description: Each joint's position, in the order of joints.

objects.description: Every scene object's pose, sorted by name.

SceneState.description: A context's scene: the objects it can hold and what it holds now.

revision.description: Increments on every change, from 0 when the context opens.

objects.description: Scene objects that can be attached, sorted.

fixtures.description: Static scene bodies an attachment may allow contact with, sorted.

Submission.description: A command accepted by a context for execution, with its source and deadline.

execution.description: Execution identifier assigned by the context.

deadline.description: Runtime time by which it must finish, else it times out.

snapshot.description: Fingerprint of the snapshot the command was planned on, if given.

prepared.description: Fingerprint of the PreparedTrajectory the command was compiled as, when RobotContext.execute submitted it; the trace's preceding compiled record.

Timestamp.description: A point in time on a named clock.

TraceRecord.description: One event in a context's life, in causal order.

clock.description: Clock of time_ns: the runtime clock.

source.description: Who caused it: a submitter, 'context', or 'runtime:<name>'.

TrajectoryContract.description: How a runtime executes a ``JointTrajectory``: the trajectory-execution contract a

interpolation.description: How the runtime moves between waypoints.

fixed_period.description: Whether the period holds for the lifetime of the context.

goal_tolerance.description: How close, per joint, a trajectory's end must be reached for it to succeed; None when the runtime declares none.

Tsr.description: A task space region: the poses ``origin @ T_w @ offset`` with ``T_w`` within the

origin.description: The region frame's pose in the world (T0_w).

offset.description: The constrained frame in the region frame (Tw_e).

position_bounds.description: Lower and upper x, y, z in the region frame.

rotation_bounds.description: Lower and upper roll, pitch, yaw.

TsrGoal.description: Bring the request's frame into any one of these regions.

ValidationPolicy.description: What a validator checks, how, and what its answer guarantees. The guarantee is

resolution.description: Largest joint-space step between checked states; required for a discrete policy.

parameters.description: Every other mechanism setting, as sorted (key, value) pairs.

ValidatorIdentity.description: Which validator answered, under which policy, for which scene and constraints.

snapshot.description: Fingerprint of the scene snapshot it is bound to.

group.description: The joint group whose motions it validates.

constraints.description: Fingerprint of the constraints it applies; see constraints_identity.

goal.description: Fingerprint of the goal its goal_distance measures; see goal_identity.

WrenchGuard.description: A force-torque condition a runtime evaluates at every control tick.

axis.description: Unit axis in the sensor frame to project onto; None for the magnitude.

threshold.description: Trigger when the measure reaches this.

tare.description: Measure from the reading when the motion started.

samples.description: Consecutive ticks at or over the threshold.
